gen_risks.description: Geopolitical instability and regional macroeconomic shocks in the MENA region could suppress private capital flows and investor confidence, threatening capital mobilization targets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Structure ISSF investments to provide matching co-investments on commercial non-subsidized terms to de-risk private VC entry, while serving as a strategic co-investment partner to regional/GCC funds.
gen_risks.evidence: Section I.A, para 1: Jordan’s small, open economy continues to face vulnerabilities tied to its position in a geopolitically volatile region.

gen_risks.description: High-growth Jordanian startups may relocate headquarters to GCC or Western markets to access larger growth capital, reducing local economic and employment impact.
gen_risks.mitigation: Contractually enforce Side Letters with partner VC funds requiring portfolio companies to maintain significant commercial operations and workforce footprint in Jordan.
gen_risks.evidence: Section I.B, para 7: Availability of long-term funding and market size in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries... prompt high-growth Jordanian startups to expand elsewhere

gen_risks.description: Expansion of ICT and technology startups supported by the fund could lead to improper management and disposal of e-waste, causing environmental pollution and health hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate E&S screening into sub-project approval, enforce e-waste management clauses in Fund legal documentation, and promote adoption of good e-waste recycling practices.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.C, para 77: SMEs’ supported activities may cause environmental impacts connected to mismanagement of e-waste, including pollution, Occupational Health and Safety

gen_risks.description: Growing ICT startups could lack formal human resources policies, leading to labor standard violations, discrimination, or sexual harassment in the workplace.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement ESCP gap-filling measures aligning beneficiary practices with national labor law and ESS2, adopt workplace non-discrimination policies, and enforce anti-harassment standards.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.C, para 78: Additional labor risks related to ICT start-ups include terms and conditions of employment, discrimination, and sexual harassment

gen_risks.description: The existing Grievance Mechanism (GM) at ISSF may lack sufficient reach or specialized procedures to address SEA/SH complaints and broader stakeholder concerns effectively.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enhance GM protocols to establish safe, confidential, survivor-centered uptake channels for SEA/SH and extend accessible grievance reporting mechanisms across all sub-projects.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.C, para 82: according to a recent E&S audit for ISSF, it was found that the GM system requires enhancement

gen_risks.description: Over-concentration of investable capital into a single VC fund or startup could lead to disproportionate portfolio losses if the counterparty underperforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate strict nominal and percentage exposure caps in the Project Operations Manual (e.g., maximum US$5 million cap and no more than 15% loan size per fund).
gen_risks.evidence: Section II.D, para 34: To mitigate and manage concentration risks, the current ISSF Investment Strategy sets out the limit on ISSF investment in one VC fund.

gen_risks.description: An acute shortage of pre-seed and seed financing could bottleneck the pipeline of deal-ready startups moving toward early and growth stage venture rounds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Ring-fence approximately 30 percent of total investable capital under Component 1 specifically for pre-seed and seed stage funds, incubators, and accelerators.
gen_risks.evidence: Section II.D, para 33: pre-seed and seed funding are in short supply.

gen_risks.description: ISSF and financial intermediaries may lack sufficient capacity to evaluate and manage Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) requirements and standard ESMS implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint dedicated E&S staff within the ISSF PMU, mandate that all recipient VC funds establish an approved ESMS, and provide continuous institutional capacity building.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.C, para 79: ISSF requires improved E&S risks and impacts management capacity, especially in the implementation of the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards

gen_risks.description: Private VC funds and startups could fail to comply with acceptable commercial procurement practices or misprice sub-contracts, causing fiduciary compliance failures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit a qualified procurement specialist for the PMU, outline explicit commercial practices in the POM, perform annual ex-post reviews, and engage independent technical auditors.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.B, para 73: ISSF shall satisfy itself with the reasonableness of the price of contracts awarded, through the hiring of independent auditors

gen_risks.description: The legal structure of ISSF as a Private Shareholding Company set to expire in 2029 conflicts with standard 10–12 year venture capital investment cycles.
gen_risks.mitigation: Execute a legal amendment to ISSF's Articles of Association as an effectiveness condition to convert ISSF into an open-ended Private Shareholding Company.
gen_risks.evidence: Section II.D, para 30(vii): currently the ISSF Private Shareholding Company ‘ends’ in 2029

gen_risks.description: Relying on external lead investors for due diligence under Component 2 co-investments could expose ISSF to flawed valuations or excessive aggregate exposure to single startups.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish strict double-exposure checks across Component 1 and 2 in the POM, cap co-investments at US$500,000, and ensure independent review by the Investment Committee.
gen_risks.evidence: Section II.D, para 36: consider the risks related to total exposure to the same startups (through Component 1 and Component 2)

gen_risks.description: Deep-seated social norms and systemic barriers could prevent female and youth entrepreneurs from equitably accessing early-stage risk capital.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a Gender Action Plan with targeted outreach, mandate at least 20% female representation on the Board and Investment Committee, and target >=30% female-led/owned beneficiaries.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.C, para 78: there is a risk that they may not fully benefit if specific barriers to their participation are not effectively addressed.

gen_risks.description: Sub-project funding could inadvertently support business activities that are non-aligned with Paris Agreement objectives or increase national mitigation/adaptation vulnerabilities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update the ISSF Investment Strategy and POM to include universal Paris Alignment exclusion lists and counterparty/transaction screening procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV.A, para 56: ISSF Investment Strategy will be updated to amend the exclusion list with activities that are universally non-aligned from Paris Alignment perspective.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is rated Substantial. External economic shocks, regional instability and related uncertainties, or a downturn in global venture capital markets could reduce investor confidence and slow private capital mobilization. Additionally, Jordan's nascent venture capital market and competition from more developed ecosystems in neighboring countries may impact startup retention and funding.

Other risks are rated Substantial and relate to geopolitical risk. Jordan's strategic location makes it susceptible to a complex set of geopolitical challenges that have intensified in recent years, due to the current Conflict in the Middle East and its repercussions for investment, trade, and tourism in the region. Increasing geopolitical risks may prompt adjustments in policy and budgetary priorities and/or contribute to delays in implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: By combining regional and global diplomacy, building international partnerships, staying the course on political and economic modernization reforms, implementing prudent fiscal policies, and strategic security measures, Jordan has maintained its resilience and stability despite continuous crises.
